headline: LIBERTY GOLD DELIVERS BLACK PINE FEASIBILITY — $2.4B NPV, 4M OZ RESERVE, 60% IRR IN IDAHO
snippet: Liberty Gold (TSX: LGD) released a Feasibility Study at its 100%-owned Black Pine Oxide Gold Project in southern Idaho on September 8, 2026, outlining a base-case after-tax NPV of US$2.4 billion and a 60.5% IRR at a US$3,250/oz gold price, against initial capital of US$411 million — a 4.04 million oz Au Probable Mineral Reserve, 16-year mine life, and average annual production of 176,700 oz, rising to 202,000 oz during years 1–5 in a technically simple run-of-mine heap-leach operation requiring no ore crushing, screening or agglomeration. At today's ~$4,400 gold price rather than the $3,250 base case, the project economics improve materially, positioning Black Pine as one of the most capital-efficient undeveloped oxide gold projects in the western U.S.

headline: POWER METALLIC'S MAIDEN LION RESOURCE: 4.75 MT AT 3.9% CuEq — 406M LBS WITH PGMs, 87% INDICATED
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) announced on September 8, 2026 the inaugural Mineral Resource Estimate for the Lion Zone at its Nisk Project in Eeyou Istchee James Bay, Québec: 4,145,000 tonnes Indicated at 3.86% CuEq plus 601,000 tonnes Inferred at 4.01% CuEq — totalling approximately 406 million pounds of copper equivalent, including 80,500 tonnes of copper, 528,000 oz of platinum group metals, and 72,000 oz of gold, with more than 85% classified as Indicated. Locked-cycle metallurgical tests returned copper recoveries above 98% producing concentrates grading over 25% Cu; five rigs remain active targeting depth and strike extensions with summer 2026 assays expected from September onward.

headline: DPM METALS HITS 246M AT 1.36% CuEq IN SERBIA — DUMITRU POTOK EXTENDS 90M WEST; 15 RIGS BY YEAR-END
snippet: DPM Metals Inc. (TSX/ASX: DPM) released September 8, 2026 drill results from Dumitru Potok on its Čoka Rakita exploration licence in Serbia: hole BIDD253 returned 246 metres grading 1.36% CuEq (0.67% Cu, 0.69 g/t Au, 4.21 g/t Ag), including a 26-metre sub-interval at 2.07% CuEq, extending marble-hosted skarn mineralization approximately 90 metres west and 100 metres southwest of the existing resource boundary. The company is expanding the 2026 program to 32,000–35,000 metres with plans to deploy 15 total rigs at Čoka Rakita by year-end; an updated resource estimate is targeted for Q1 2027 to form the basis of a PEA by end-2027.

headline: URANIUM HITS $89/LB AS KAZATOMPROM SLASHES OUTPUT 10% — JUNIOR MINERS UP 21.75% IN SEPTEMBER
snippet: Spot uranium rebounded to approximately $89 per pound in early September 2026, with junior uranium miners posting gains of 21.75% month-to-date, as Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom — the world's largest uranium producer — confirmed a roughly 10% reduction in its 2026 nominal production target to approximately 29,697 tU from a planned 32,777 tU, citing sulphuric acid supply constraints. Cameco's previously disclosed McArthur River production cut compounds the shortfall, reinforcing a structural deficit that the World Nuclear Association projects will intensify through the decade as SMR deployments and new reactor capacity more than double uranium requirements by 2040.

headline: VALE SCRAPS BASE METALS IPO — BRAZIL POLITICS FORCE INDEFINITE DELAY ON CRITICAL MINERALS SPINOUT
snippet: Vale has shelved plans for an initial public offering of its Vale Base Metals subsidiary — which holds its nickel, copper, and cobalt operations — indefinitely, according to The Globe and Mail, citing political opposition in Brazil to ceding control of strategic mineral assets ahead of the October 2026 presidential election. CEO Shaun Usmar had targeted mid-2026 IPO readiness; Vale filed a 6-K with the SEC on September 8 while publicly stating it does not comment on "market rumors and speculation." The decision removes a near-term catalyst that had been expected to crystallize the value of Vale's battery metals portfolio at a time when nickel and copper prices are historically elevated.

headline: STANMORE SECURES 724 MILLION TONNE MORANBAH SOUTH MET COAL FOR US$105M FROM EXXARO
snippet: Stanmore Resources agreed on September 8, 2026 to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million (A$145 million), following a three-party structure in which Exxaro first acquired Anglo American's 50% stake in the Grosvenor JV before selling the whole package to Stanmore. The tenements contain 724 million tonnes measured and indicated in the Goonyella Middle Seam — expected to be premium hard coking coal quality — adjacent to Stanmore's Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects with potential for shared infrastructure. Completion is expected before year-end 2026, subject to FIRB, ACCC and Queensland ministerial approvals.

headline: GOLD SLIPS TO $4,385 AS OIL SHOCK PUTS THURSDAY PPI IN FED CROSSHAIRS — RATE HIKE ODDS NEAR 60%
snippet: Gold fell 0.4% to around $4,385 on September 9, 2026 as rising oil prices compounded inflation concerns and reinforced Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations, with markets now pricing approximately 60% odds of a hike at the September 16 meeting. Producer Price Index data is due Thursday and Consumer Price Index data Friday — both prints will determine whether the rate narrative shifts before the Fed meeting; silver held near $66.30. Gold bulls argue that any hike forcing a growth slowdown will ultimately trigger the easing cycle that underpins the structural debasement trade, setting up an oversold-recovery entry.

headline: FOUR RIGS TURNING AT PECOY COPPER — 35,000M PERU PORPHYRY RAMPING AFTER 804M HIT AT 0.34% Cu
snippet: Pecoy Copper Corp. (TSX-V: PCU) reported on September 8, 2026 that four diamond drill rigs are now active at its Pecoy Copper-Gold-Molybdenum-Silver Project in southern Peru, with a fifth rig planned. The operational update follows the company's September 1 assay release that included hole PEC26-072 intersecting 804 metres at 0.34% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au from 24 metres depth at the South Breccia, and hole PEC26-067 returning 42.3 metres at 1.01% Cu at the Northwest target — results that define a large, near-surface porphyry system at a moment when LME copper is trading above $14,700 per tonne.

headline: PANORO EXTENDS COTABAMBAS SOUTH PIT TO 1,100M DEPTH — 808M AT 0.31% CuEq CONFIRMS PERU PORPHYRY SCALE
snippet: Panoro Minerals (TSX-V: PML) released assay results from drill holes CB-229 and CB-230 at the Cotabambas Project in Apurímac, Peru, with CB-230 intersecting 808.15 metres of hypogene mineralization at 0.31% CuEq — including 156.5 metres at 0.55% CuEq and a 48.1-metre zone at 0.76% CuEq — extending continuous copper-gold porphyry mineralization at the South Pit to approximately 1,100 metres depth and 600 metres along strike. The results validate the hypothesis of a large, open porphyry system at depth across the 165 km² project, with Panoro pursuing parallel goals of resource extension in the North and South areas and broader regional discovery.

headline: SILVER'S UNSUNG STRENGTH: UP 116% YEAR-OVER-YEAR IN 2026 AS MAINSTREAM FOCUS STAYS ON GOLD SELLOFF
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis highlights that despite trading down from its 2026 highs alongside gold, silver has averaged nearly $74 per ounce year-to-date in 2026 — a phenomenal 116.7% above the comparable 2025 period — while media coverage has fixated on gold's decline from its January $5,419 record. China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material, six consecutive supply deficits, and the metal's dual monetary and industrial role in solar panels and EVs underpin a case that silver's current weakness near $66.30 is a dislocation, not a structural reversal — with Silvercorp's forced 40-50% output cut in China from safety inspections adding a fresh supply-side catalyst.

headline: GALLOPER GOLD SPINS UP 7,000M AT GLOVER ISLAND — 30-HOLE NEWFOUNDLAND PROGRAM LAUNCHES
snippet: Galloper Gold Corp. (CSE: BOOM) commenced NQ diamond drilling at its flagship Glover Island property in Newfoundland & Labrador, launching a planned 7,000-metre, 30-hole 2026 exploration program targeting high-priority gold zones identified through prior surface work and geological mapping. Glover Island occupies a significant portion of the Central Newfoundland gold belt — a belt that has attracted renewed exploration capital as discovery-stage juniors benefit from elevated gold prices near $4,400 per ounce and investor appetite for pre-results drill stories.
